column1: # dta_stub_registry.tsv — source of truth for native/src/dta_link_stubs.s
#   kind  in {func, data} (dta_link_stubs.s currently has no genuine `data` rows —
#     invariant: kind=data => class=data-blob ; kind=func => class in
#   note  free text (safety justification for ok-noop rows; boot-hit provenance)
# Seeding rule (W0.2.S4, behavior-preserving MOVE): unknown => assert-unreachable
# (conservative), matching band3_stub_registry.tsv's S1 rule. Every row here was
# seeded assert-unreachable; promotions to ok-noop happen only from measured
# boot-smoke evidence (mirrors S3's methodology), not from guessing.
# SHAPE NOTE: unlike band3_link_stubs.s, this file's typeinfo/vtable symbols
# (_ZTI*/_ZTV*/_ZTT*/_ZThn64_*) are NOT given their own writable .bss reservation
# today — they alias the same read-only .text no-op stub as ordinary functions.
# That is almost certainly a latent bug if anything ever WRITES through one of
# them (band3's own history records exactly that crash pattern for its data
# stubs), but reclassifying them to kind=data (own .bss) would be a BEHAVIOR
# CHANGE, out of scope for this registry-extraction MOVE. They are seeded here
# with kind=func (matching current shape) so regeneration is byte-behavior-
# identical; flag for a follow-up item if one is ever observed being written.
# EXCLUDED FROM THIS REGISTRY: _Z12EndianSwapEqIiEvRT_ (EndianSwapEq<int>) is a
# REAL strong implementation (a faithful in-place 4-byte byteswap, __rb3_endian_
# swap_eq_int), not a no-op stub — it is preserved verbatim by the generator's
# per-set SPECIAL_VERBATIM block, not driven by a registry row.
